neighbours.label: the article or 'and' right after a verb of formally granting or imposing something, before the thing bestowed, in historical / legal narrative: 'gave Nixon a | pardon', 'honours and | offices', 'swear an | oath'
fire: In 1215 the barons forced the king to grant them a charter of liberties.
The pope received the pilgrims and gave them a solemn blessing.
After the trial the governor issued the prisoner a full reprieve.
The council voted the admiral a pension and a sword of honour.
Each new knight was required to take an oath of fealty.
The tribunal condemned him with a unanimous verdict of guilt.
The queen rewarded the captain and gave him a knighthood.
By decree the senate awarded the consul a triumph and a statue.
quiet: In 1215 the barons forced the king to flee across a muddy river.
The pope received the pilgrims and walked through a quiet garden.
After the trial the governor rode home along a narrow lane.
The council watched the admiral cross a bridge and a square.
Each new knight was required to ride an old grey horse.
The tribunal sat for a week in a cold stone hall.
The queen greeted the captain and saw a storm approaching.
By evening the senate building was a ruin and a memory.

notes: Probes were weak (0.22-0.43 of max) and an everyday gift ('gave him a towel') still scored 0.11, so this may not reach the bar. The + pole promotes 'deliver / personally present', which looks like the other side: handing over in person versus being granted.
